column12: Judgement: house convention. Pembrolizumab is the comparator arm of ARTEMIDE-Lung02, -Lung03 and -Lung04 and is the PD-1 antibody rilvegostomig would replace; the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds carry the same anchor. The case for lower: AstraZeneca's own Imfinzi reads $56,999 (Part B 2024), the anchor the volrustomig seed uses, and Merck expects US biosimilar competition to Keytruda from December 2028 and loss of European exclusivity in 2031 (Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063, risk factors, in the book's filing_sections), which would pull the reference price down before a 2032 first full year. The case for higher: a per-beneficiary figure covers less than a full year of therapy for many patients (adjuvant courses, deaths, stops), so it understates an annual price, and a new bispecific winning on overall survival could launch at a premium

column11: KEYNOTE-189 (Gandhi et al., N Engl J Med 2018;378:2078, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1801005, PMID 29658856): median PFS 8.8 months (95% CI 7.6 to 9.2) on pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, the control regimen of ARTEMIDE-Lung03 (NCT06627647), the largest of the three lung trials at 1,160 patients
column12: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/8.8) = 0.611, the form the ABBV-1480, PF-08634404 and sigvotatug vedotin seeds use (the brief's 1 - exp(-12/8.8) gives 0.744 but treats the median as a mean). Judgement on which control arm: non-squamous is about 75% of known histology in the Chen et al. cohort (67.9% against 22.5%). The other two trials' control arms give 0.727 (KEYNOTE-407, squamous, median PFS 6.4 months, Paz-Ares et al., N Engl J Med 2018;379:2040, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1810865) and 0.554 (KEYNOTE-024, PD-L1 50% or more, 10.3 months, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1606774, the sigvotatug vedotin seed's source). The case for lower: the trials are designed to extend survival over pembrolizumab, and patients who respond stay on longer than the median implies; KEYNOTE-189's five-year update (Garassino et al., J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1992, doi:10.1200/JCO.22.01989) shows 57 of 410 completing all 35 cycles

column12: Judgement: the book's convention of the first full year two calendar years after primary completion (the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds), applied to Lung04, the first rilvegostomig-alone lung trial to complete: readout in 2030, filing in 2030 and approval around 2031. The chemotherapy trials that carry most of the pool complete later in 2030, so their labels would follow about a year after. The case for earlier: TROPION-Lung10 (NCT06357533), Datroway plus rilvegostomig against pembrolizumab in TROP2-positive, PD-L1-high non-squamous NSCLC, completes 2029-12-28, which the same convention would put at 2031, but it is a combination in a biomarker subset. Other indications complete earlier (adjuvant biliary NCT06109779 2029-01-02, DESTINY-Endometrial01 NCT06989112 2029-01-19) and are not modelled here

column12: Judgement on the rate: a royalty AstraZeneca pays, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin = (0.274667 - 0.05) / 0.274667 = 0.8180, reading 'up to mid-single digits' as 5% on the top tier where a large product's sales mostly fall. The exact tiers are not disclosed. At 4% the share is 0.8544, at 6% 0.7816. The case for a higher share: the royalty is tiered and 'up to', so early and lower-tier sales pay less. Milestones of up to $195mm to Compugen are not in this field. No other partner: AstraZeneca is lead sponsor of every rilvegostomig trial in the book

column11: Four filters multiplied, each already in the book: 55% advanced or metastatic at presentation (the volrustomig seed); 81.6% without an alteration carrying a first-line targeted therapy (Wang et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2026, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2025.7131, the PF-08634404 seed's share); 79% starting first-line therapy, 2,904 of 3,661 US stage IV patients without EGFR or ALK alterations (Abernethy et al., PLoS One 2017, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0178420, the ABBV-1480 seed's share); and 77.8% with PD-L1 of 1% or more, about 3,770 of 4,848 first-line-treated US patients with a quantified result (Leapman et al., JAMA Netw Open 2020;3(6):e207205, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.7205, PMID 32511721, the PF-08046054 seed's share). 0.55 x 0.816 x 0.79 x 0.778 = 0.2758, about 53,100 patients a year
column12: The label union of the three lung trials: Lung02 and Lung03 enrol squamous and non-squamous first-line metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TC 1% or more (J Thorac Oncol 2025 P3.18.35; J Clin Oncol 2025 TPS8653), and Lung04 enrols PD-L1 high, a subset of that. PD-L1-negative patients (about 22%) are outside every trial. The case against: the driver filter is applied to squamous tumours too, where actionable alterations are rare, which slightly understates; the 55% counts only advanced disease at presentation and misses recurrence after early-stage treatment, which also understates; and PD-L1 status and driver status are not independent, which cuts the other way

column11: Pembrolizumab, the incumbent: in 8,811 US patients with advanced NSCLC starting treatment 2015 to 2021, the five most common first-line regimens in stage IV, 64.4% of all first-line therapy, were all pembrolizumab alone or with platinum chemotherapy (Chen et al., Innov Pharm 2025;16(3), doi:10.24926/iip.v16i3.6702, PMID 42256417, the paper the ABBV-1480 seed uses for histology). 0.644 x 0.5 = 0.322
column12: Judgement: half the incumbent's measured share, the multiple the verified sigvotatug vedotin seed takes. Rilvegostomig is a like-for-like swap for pembrolizumab in the same regimens, so pembrolizumab's share is its ceiling if it wins on overall survival. The case for higher: 64.4% is a floor, since it counts only the top five regimens, includes driver-positive patients treated with targeted drugs, and averages in 2015 and 2016 before first-line approval; Leapman et al. found 83.5% of PD-L1-high first-line patients received an ICI by 2016 to 2018. The case for lower: the slot will be crowded by 2032, with PD-1/VEGF bispecifics (ivonescimab, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480), AstraZeneca's own volrustomig in PD-L1 below 50%, and pembrolizumab biosimilars from December 2028 (Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063), which make the incumbent cheap just as rilvegostomig launches; and the anti-TIGIT mechanism has no approved precedent, so even an overall survival win may meet caution. The book's other first-line lung seeds (volrustomig, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480) carry 0.2 without a measured anchor. Case lower, from the second reader: if rilvegostomig does not beat pembrolizumab and AstraZeneca mostly switches its own checkpoint patients, the capture is 0.02 (Imjudo's 1,259 Part B beneficiaries over the 53,141 eligible) to 0.13 (pembrolizumab's share scaled by the Imfinzi franchise against Keytruda); the probability of success already carries that failure case, so 0.322 is the peak if it wins
